title: LG Dishwasher AE Error Code: Leak Detected and How to Fix
meta_description: AE on an LG dishwasher means water has reached the base tray and the leak float has tripped. Stop using it, find the drip, dry the pan.
h1: LG dishwasher AE error code: water in the base, and how to find the leak
answer: AE means your LG dishwasher has detected water where water should never be: in the shallow metal tray under the tub. A foam float sits in that tray, and when water lifts it, the control stops the cycle and usually runs the drain pump to protect the house. It is a real leak nine times out of ten, not a sensor glitch, so the machine should stay off until you find where the water is coming from. Drying the tray will clear the code, but it comes straight back on the next cycle if the leak is still there.
time_estimate: 45 minutes to find it, 1 to 3 hours to fix it
safety_warning: You are working around water and a 120V appliance. Switch the dishwasher off at the breaker, not just at the panel, before you pull it out or reach into the base. Do not run the machine with the toe kick off to watch for the leak unless the power is off and you are only filling it by hand.

causes.cause: A seal at the sump or circulation pump is weeping
causes.confirm: Dry the base tray completely, put a sheet of paper towel under the middle of the machine, and run a short cycle. If the towel wets in the center, under the round sump housing rather than near the door or the sides, the leak is at the sump gasket or a pump seal.

causes.cause: The door gasket or the lower door seal is leaking
causes.confirm: Water tracks down the inside of the door and onto the floor in front of the machine, and the paper towel wets at the very front of the base tray first. Run your finger around the gasket: a flat, hardened or torn section, or a gap at a lower corner, is the spot.

causes.cause: A hose clamp or hose joint under the machine is dripping
causes.confirm: With the toe kick off and a flashlight, look at where the fill hose meets the inlet valve, where the drain hose leaves the pump, and the thick corrugated hose that feeds the upper spray arm. A drip here leaves a clean streak on a dusty hose and a wet patch directly below it.

causes.cause: Too much detergent, or the wrong detergent, foaming over
causes.confirm: You see suds through the door window or a cuff of foam around the door when you open it mid cycle. This happens after someone puts hand dish soap in the dispenser, or after a pre-rinse in a sink full of washing-up liquid carries soap in on the dishes.

causes.cause: The float is stuck up, or the float switch has failed
causes.confirm: The base tray is bone dry, there is no sign of water anywhere, and AE still appears within a minute of starting. Dried detergent crust or a bit of broken glass can hold the float up, and a failed switch reads as tripped with nothing touching it.

causes.cause: A cracked sump, tub seam or heater element seal
causes.confirm: The leak comes back after you have replaced gaskets and tightened clamps, and the wet patch is directly under the plastic sump body or under the heater element bulkhead rather than at any joint. This is the point at which the repair often costs more than the machine is worth.

steps.name: Stop the cycle and cut the power and water
steps.detail: Press Power to end the cycle, then switch off the dishwasher at the breaker. Reach under the sink and close the small isolation valve on the hot line that feeds the machine, usually a quarter-turn lever or a round handle on the supply before the braided hose. This stops any ongoing leak while you work and makes the rest of the job safe.
steps.warning: Breaker off, not just the panel. The control board is live whenever the circuit is on.

steps.name: Remove the toe kick and look into the base
steps.detail: The toe kick is the panel across the bottom front, held by two or four Phillips screws at each end or in the middle. Take it off and shine a flashlight into the shallow metal tray underneath the tub. Expect standing water of anywhere from a teaspoon to half an inch. Note where the water is deepest, because that is your first clue to the source.

steps.name: Dry the base tray and free the float
steps.detail: Soak the tray dry with a sponge and old towels, working the towel to the back as far as you can reach. Find the foam float, a small block of white or colored foam sitting in a plastic guide near the front of the tray, and lift it with a finger. It should rise about an inch and drop back under its own weight. If it sticks, clean the guide with a damp cloth to clear dried detergent, then check it drops freely.

steps.name: Run a paper towel leak trace
steps.detail: Lay strips of paper towel across the floor of the base tray, front to back and side to side, so each area of the tray has its own strip. Put the power and water back on and run the shortest cycle you have. Stop it as soon as AE appears, or after about ten minutes, and pull the strips out one at a time. The first strip to wet tells you whether the leak is at the door, the sump in the middle, or a hose at one side.
steps.warning: Keep hands clear of the base while power is on. Read the strips with the breaker off again.

steps.name: Inspect the door gasket and the lower door seal
steps.detail: Open the door fully. Run a finger all the way around the gasket set into the tub opening and along the strip at the bottom edge of the door. You are feeling for a hardened section that no longer springs back, a tear, a gap at a lower corner, or a piece of the gasket that has popped out of its groove. Push any loose section back into the channel and press the whole length of the gasket back in evenly.

steps.name: Check the hose connections under the machine
steps.detail: With the toe kick still off and the power off, work along every hose you can see. Nip up the spring clamps on the drain hose where it leaves the pump and where it joins the house drain, check that the braided fill hose is tight at the inlet valve, and look at the thick corrugated hose that runs up the side of the tub. A drip leaves a clean trail on a dusty hose. Tighten by hand or with pliers; do not overdo a plastic fitting.

steps.name: Rule out suds before you order any part
steps.detail: If you saw foam in the tub, run one empty cycle with no detergent at all and watch through the window. A half cup of white vinegar in the bottom of the tub helps knock the foam down. Then switch to a dishwasher powder or a sealed tablet, and stop any habit of rinsing plates in soapy water before loading. Suds can push water over the tub lip and into the base with nothing at all wrong with the machine.

steps.name: Dry the tray again and reset
steps.detail: Once the leak is fixed, the tray still has to be dry for the code to clear. Sponge it out, then leave the toe kick off and a fan blowing at the opening for an hour if you cannot reach the back of the tray. Switch the breaker off for five minutes and back on, then run a short cycle to test. An AE that comes back on the first cycle after a genuine repair means the tray was still damp, or there are two leaks.

still_showing: If the base tray is dry, the float drops freely, the gasket looks good and AE comes straight back, work through it in this order. First, rule out the float circuit itself: with the breaker off, unplug the two-wire connector at the float switch and look for green corrosion or a pushed-back pin, which is the cheapest possible outcome and common in a damp cabinet. A continuity check across the switch with the float down should read closed or open consistently, and a switch that reads tripped with nothing touching it is dead. The float switch is a cheap part and a twenty-minute job. Second, if the switch is fine, you have a leak you have not found yet, and the usual hiding place is the junction between the plastic sump and the bottom of the steel tub, which is sealed by a large ring gasket you cannot see without taking the sump apart. The tell is a wet patch dead center in the base tray after a cycle, with everything at the door and the hoses dry. Third, check the upper spray arm feed where it passes through the back wall of the tub, and the heater element bulkhead seals, both of which weep slowly and only under pressure, so they look perfect when the machine is idle. Fourth, if your machine is more than about eight years old and the leak is at the sump body or a tub seam rather than a replaceable gasket, get a quote before you commit: a sump assembly plus labor often lands close to the price of a new mid-range dishwasher. One thing worth checking before any of that, because it costs nothing: look at whether the machine is sitting level and not tipped forward. A dishwasher that has dropped at the front, often after a floor was replaced and the feet were never reset, lets water pool against the door seal and run out of the bottom corner on every cycle, and no amount of new gasket will fix it.
reset_procedure: Switch the dishwasher off at the breaker for five minutes, then back on. Pressing Power alone will not clear a stored AE on most models. The code will not stay cleared unless the base tray is actually dry and the float has dropped, so dry the tray first and reset second. If AE returns within seconds of powering up, the float is still raised or stuck, not the control.
model_notes: The AE code behaves the same across LG's front-control and top-control dishwashers, but the leak hardware differs slightly. Most models use a foam float and a small reed or microswitch in the base tray. Some later models add a second moisture sensor and will also close an inlet valve at the supply, which means the machine will not fill at all until the fault is cleared. On a model with LG's ThinQ app, a separate cloud alert can appear as SmDg-AE; that is a notification generated from the machine's data, not a different fault, and it points at the same base tray.

parts.name: Base tray float switch
parts.note: Only needed when the tray is dry and the switch reads tripped

parts.name: Door perimeter gasket
parts.note: Presses into a channel; no tools beyond patience on most models

parts.name: Lower door seal or baffle strip
parts.note: Common wear item and a frequent cause of water in front of the machine

parts.name: Sump gasket kit
parts.note: Means laying the machine on its back and splitting the sump from the tub

parts.name: Circulation pump assembly
parts.note: Last resort, and only when the leak is traced to the pump body itself

when_to_call: Call someone if you have dried the tray, confirmed the float moves freely, checked the door gasket and every hose clamp, and the tray still fills on a cycle. At that point the leak is inside the sump, the pump or the tub itself, and tracing it means laying the machine on its back with the plumbing disconnected. Call sooner if you can see water getting to anything electrical, if the machine trips the breaker, or if there is water under the adjacent cabinet or a soft patch in the floor, because at that point the water damage costs more than the repair. Get a quote before agreeing to a sump or pump replacement on a machine over eight years old; the parts and labor often approach the cost of a new one.

faqs.q: Can I still use my LG dishwasher with an AE code?
faqs.a: No. AE means water is sitting in the base tray, which is one pan of water away from the floor and the cabinets. The machine will shut the cycle down anyway, and forcing it through resets just pumps more water into the leak. Turn it off, close the supply valve under the sink, and wash by hand until you have found the source.

faqs.q: Why does AE come back after I dried the base?
faqs.a: Because drying the tray clears the symptom, not the cause. The float drops, the code goes, then the next cycle puts water back in the tray within minutes. If AE returns on the first cycle after a dry-out, you have a live leak. If it returns only after several loads, the leak is slow, which usually points at a gasket rather than a hose joint.

faqs.q: Does AE always mean a leak, or can the sensor be wrong?
faqs.a: A leak, most of the time. The float does occasionally stick up on dried detergent or a shard of glass, and the switch itself does fail, but both are the exception. Check the tray before you assume a sensor fault: if there is any water in it at all, believe the machine. A dry tray plus an instant AE on power-up points at the float.

faqs.q: Can too much detergent cause an AE error?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is more common than people expect. Hand dish soap in the dispenser, or plates rinsed in a sink of soapy water, generates foam that climbs over the tub lip into the base tray. Run one empty cycle with no detergent and a half cup of vinegar to clear it, then use dishwasher powder or tablets only.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to fix an AE error on an LG dishwasher?
faqs.a: Nothing at all if it is suds or a loose clamp. A door gasket or float switch runs roughly $20 to $60 in parts and an hour of your time. A sump gasket or pump seal is a technician job at around $150 to $400 fitted, and on a machine past eight years old that is close enough to replacement cost to be worth a conversation.

faqs.q: Why did AE appear suddenly when nothing changed?
faqs.a: Seals harden slowly and then cross a threshold, so a gasket that has been marginal for a year fails in one load. The other common trigger is something that moved the machine: a floor replacement, a new countertop, or anyone pulling it out to retrieve a dropped fork can tip it forward or nudge a hose clamp off square.

faqs.q: Should I pull the dishwasher out to find the leak?
faqs.a: Not as the first step. Take the toe kick off first, which takes four screws and shows you most of the base. Only pull the machine out if the toe kick view shows nothing and you need to see the back, and when you do, switch off the breaker, close the supply valve, and watch that the drain hose does not pull out of its standpipe.

faqs.q: Is an LG dishwasher with an AE error worth repairing?
faqs.a: It depends entirely on where the leak is. A gasket, a clamp or a float switch is worth fixing on any machine. A cracked sump or a leaking pump body on a machine older than about eight years usually is not, because the fitted cost lands in the same bracket as a new mid-range dishwasher with a fresh warranty.
